subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` block explicit Gateway control-plane `update.run` managed-service handoffs for supervised/headless launchd deployments, or remain scoped only to configured background auto-update applies?
rationale: The source path is clear, but either choice defines an operator-facing update contract: blocking `update.run` protects headless availability, while preserving current behavior keeps explicit update requests independent from the auto-update kill switch.

options.title: Honor the kill-switch for Gateway handoffs
options.body: Gate supervised Gateway-originated `update.run` managed handoffs before restart scheduling when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is truthy, and document the expanded contract.

options.title: Keep explicit update.run outside the kill-switch
options.body: Document that the env var only blocks configured automatic applies, and track launchd handoff reliability under the broader update-run reliability issues.

options.title: Add a separate explicit operator control
options.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` as-is and introduce a narrower documented policy for blocking Gateway-managed update restarts after a migration/docs decision.

recommendation.title: Honor the kill-switch for Gateway handoffs
recommendation.body: Gate supervised Gateway-originated `update.run` managed handoffs before restart scheduling when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is truthy, and document the expanded contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product-contract level across the core updater and Gateway restart flow, both areas tied to steipete's earlier feature history.
